findings.label: Suppliers with Current Red Flags
findings.detail: 8 current suppliers have Companies House compliance issues (historical payments were made before breaches started)

findings.label: Suspected Split Payments
findings.detail: 470 instances of 3+ payments just below approval thresholds in the same week
findings.context_note: Split payment detection has a high false-positive rate. Batch processing, staged invoices, and legitimate recurring payments can all trigger this pattern. FOI request for procurement approval chain recommended before drawing conclusions.

findings.label: Round-Number Payments (>£5K)
findings.detail: 932 exact round-number payments over £5,000 — may indicate estimates rather than invoiced amounts

findings.label: Year-End Spending Pattern
findings.detail: Substance Misuse spent 4.5x their monthly average in March (£3.0M above normal). Note: UK councils operate on April–March fiscal years, so elevated March spending is common as departments finalise annual budgets. Spikes above 3x warrant further scrutiny.
findings.context_note: March spending above the monthly average is expected for UK councils on April–March fiscal years. Compare against prior years' March figures for meaningful analysis.

findings.label: Rapid Payment Suppliers
findings.detail: 15 suppliers receive payments every <14 days on average. Top: Jewson Limited T/A : Stark Building Materials Uk Ltd (2.6 day avg, 1350 payments, £2.1M)

findings.label: Benford's Law Anomaly
findings.detail: Significant deviation from Benford's Law (p < 0.001). Digit 2 deviates 6.6% from expected distribution across 218,731 transactions. Note: with 218,731 transactions, chi-squared tests are highly sensitive — the 6.6% max digit deviation is the more practical measure of anomaly.
findings.context_note: Chi-squared values on samples of 218,731+ transactions are naturally inflated and will almost always show statistical significance. The max digit deviation (6.6%) is a more meaningful indicator — deviations under 5% are typical for legitimate council spending.

findings.label: Second-Digit Benford's Anomaly
findings.detail: Second-digit distribution across 218,731 transactions shows p < 0.001 (highly significant). Digit 3 deviates 1.4% from Nigrini's expected distribution. Second-digit tests are more discriminating than first-digit for detecting round-number bias and fabricated invoices.
findings.context_note: Benford's second-digit analysis (Nigrini, 2012) uses chi-squared with 9 df. Critical values: 16.92 (p=0.05), 21.67 (p=0.01), 27.88 (p=0.001). n=218,731.

findings.label: Weak Competition Indicators
findings.detail: 6 contracts show signs of limited competition (short tender periods or rapid award). Top: North Northamptonshire Council - Residential and N (£117.8M)
findings.context_note: Contracts Finder does not publish bid counts. These flags use proxy signals: tender periods under 14 days and awards within 7 days of deadline. Short timelines may have legitimate explanations (framework call-offs, urgency).

findings.label: Budget Category Efficiency Concerns
findings.detail: 3 service categories show multiple efficiency flags. Worst: Children Social Care (HHI=3946, 2% round-number, 0.9x year-end spike)

key_findings.title: 10 suppliers with clock-like payment regularity
key_findings.description: These suppliers receive payments at near-identical intervals (std dev <5 days). Top: Jewson Limited T/A : Stark Building Materials Uk Ltd — every 2.6 days (1350 payments, £2.1M)

key_findings.title: AROMA CARE PEOPLE: 6517 transactions totalling £7.7M
key_findings.description: Averaging £1.2K per transaction — the council's most frequent supplier

key_findings.title: 1 service categories with a single supplier
key_findings.description: Top: Civica Uk Ltd — sole winner in 'Software package and information systems' (2 contracts, £46.8K). Category monopolies may indicate market failure or specification bias.
